Ransomware Attack Disrupts New Zealand Construction Materials Firms

A sophisticated ransomware attack targeting New Zealand’s construction materials industry has caused widespread disruption, with multiple firms reporting compromised IT systems and halted operations. The cyber incident, which began late Tuesday, continues to affect supply chains, procurement, and customer services across the sector.

Firms including Southern Quarries Ltd, Pacific Concrete Solutions, and KiwiBuild Supplies have issued statements confirming their systems were encrypted by attackers demanding payment in cryptocurrency. “Our ordering platform and inventory management have been inaccessible since early this morning,” said Anna McGrath, spokesperson for Southern Quarries Ltd. “We are working with cybersecurity experts and authorities to restore operations, but at this stage, we cannot estimate when we’ll be back online.”

The attack has already resulted in significant delays in processing orders and delivering construction materials, raising concerns about ongoing building projects nationwide. “The timing is particularly challenging as the industry is already under pressure due to high demand and tight schedules,” commented Hamish Fraser, CEO of the New Zealand Construction Materials Association. “Disruption to just-in-time deliveries could set back projects by days or even weeks.”

Industry analysts estimate that over 35 percent of the sector’s firms may be experiencing operational issues linked to the incident. The Construction and General Workers Union has urged companies to prioritise staff welfare while systems are down. “We’re asking employers to keep workers informed and ensure their pay is not affected during this period,” said union secretary Moana Rangi.

The National Cyber Security Centre is coordinating the response, advising firms not to engage with ransom demands. “We are actively investigating and working to contain the threat,” a spokesperson stated. Further updates are expected as the situation develops.
